newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada spot natgas strong as storage fears arise.
newsitem.headline: Canada spot natgas strong as storage fears arise.

text.p: Canadian spot natural gas prices continued their surprising surge in Wednesday trade as marketers wondered whether storage supplies would hold out for the balance of one of the coldest winters in recent memory.
The big price jump began on Monday as western Canada and many of its export markets entered another week with frigid weather forecasted.
Effects of the cold were exacerabated by news that stocks in western Canada were at about half capacity and draining at the rate of at least 1.5 billion cubic feet per day.

The storage fears have led to sharply higher prices for both day-to-day trades and forward deals, marketers said. "If we get weather in February, storage is suspect," said a Calgary-based trader. "That's why (gas for delivery in) February has rallied so hard."
Spot gas at the AECO storage hub was talked at C$3.44 per gigajoule, up from C$2.35 last week. Gas for February delivery jumped to C$3 per GJ, from C$2.28 on January 8.

At the borders, gas for export to markets in the U.S. Midwest was pegged at over US$1 per million British thermal units above last week's levels. The Northern Plains region was socked in with the latest of several major snowstorms and Illinois utilities declared "critical days," which meant limited gas deliveries and storage withdrawals.
Temperates in the region were forecast to drop by up to 15 degrees Fahrenheit below normal starting early Thursday.
